stories.hook: ¿Por qué la psilocibina reduce más la ansiedad en mujeres?
stories.headline: Mujeres con depresión muestran menor ansiedad tras psilocibina que escitalopram
stories.finding: El análisis bayesiano de un ensayo aleatorizado de seis semanas no halló diferencias de sexo entre psilocibina y escitalopram. Sin embargo, dentro del grupo de psilocibina, las mujeres mostraron una reducción de ansiedad mayor que los hombres (diferencia ajustada = ‑8,77; intervalo creíble ‑15,73 a ‑1,73; BF = 11,18).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la psilocibina podría ofrecer un beneficio diferencial en la ansiedad para mujeres con depresión, orientando decisiones terapéuticas personalizadas y motivando investigaciones sobre mecanismos de sexo en tratamientos psicodélicos.
stories.paperTitle: Sex-related differences in outcomes following psilocybin or escitalopram: a Bayesian secondary analysis
stories.originalAbstract: RATIONALE: Major depressive disorder (MDD) shows marked sex differences in prevalence, symptomatology, and treatment response. However, females remain underrepresented in many clinical trials, and sex-specific treatment outcomes are rarely examined. OBJECTIVES: This study reanalyzed data from a randomized controlled trial comparing psilocybin and escitalopram for MDD to evaluate sex differences across multiple psychological domains. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc Bayesian analysis of a six-week, double-blind trial in adults with moderate-to-severe MDD (N = 59; 20 female; psilocybin n = 30, 11 female; escitalopram n = 29, 9 female). Post-treatment depression, anhedonia, anxiety, thought suppression, and well-being were modeled by sex, treatment, sex-by-treatment interaction, and baseline score. Sexual dysfunction, measured post-treatment only, was analyzed ordinally. Prior-sensitivity analyses used narrower and wider priors. RESULTS: No outcome showed an overall sex difference across treatments. Within psilocybin, females had lower post-treatment anxiety than males (STAI adjusted difference = -8.77, 95% CrI = -15.73 to -1.73; BFany = 11.18), although the estimate varied across priors and the narrowest prior included zero. The sex-by-treatment interaction was inconclusive (difference=-8.62, 95% CrI=-18.36 to 1.30; BFany = 2.55). A directional female advantage in anhedonia with escitalopram was unsupported by Bayes factors. No sex differences emerged on depression scales. Among males, sexual dysfunction was lower with psilocybin than with escitalopram. Within escitalopram, females reported less sexual dysfunction than males. CONCLUSIONS: This reanalysis identified sex-related patterns in anxiety under psilocybin but no clear treatment-specific interaction. Findings support adequately powered, sex-balanced trials incorporating hormonal and reproductive factors.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena reducir la rumiación al instante?
stories.headline: La atención plena desvinculada disminuye la rumiación negativa en minutos
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 50 participantes con alta rumiación, la práctica de mindfulness desvinculado redujo significativamente el RNT 15 min después (b = ‑0.26, IC 95 % = [‑0.38,‑0.14]). Los dos grupos de ejercicio (mindfulness desvinculado y control activo) no mostraron diferencias en la mejora.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que una breve práctica de mindfulness desvinculado puede aliviar rápidamente la rumiación, ofreciendo una herramienta práctica para intervenciones tempranas en trastornos de ansiedad y depresión.
stories.paperTitle: Assessing the Immediate Effects of Detached Mindfulness on Repetitive Negative Thinking and Affect in Daily Life: A Randomized Controlled Trial
stories.originalAbstract: Objectives Repetitive negative thinking (RNT) is a problematic thinking style that is related to multiple mental disorders. Detached mindfulness is a technique of metacognitive therapy that aims to reduce RNT. Our study set out to investigate the immediate effects of detached mindfulness in daily life. Methods Participants with elevated trait RNT (n = 50) were prompted to engage in detached mindfulness exercises three times a day for 5 consecutive days. Immediate effects on RNT and affect were assessed 15 and 30 min after each exercise using experience sampling methodology. We compared the effects of this exercise phase to (1) a 5-day non-exercise baseline phase and (2) a different group of participants that engaged in an active control exercise (n = 50). Results Results of Bayesian multilevel models showed that, across groups, improvements in RNT, negative affect, and positive affect were stronger during the exercise phase than during the non-exercise baseline phase (RNT after 15 min: b = -0.26, 95% CI = [-0.38, -0.14]). However, the two exercise groups did not differ in these improvements (RNT after 15 min: b = 0.02, 95% CI = [-0.22, 0.27]). Thus, the detached mindfulness and the active control exercises resulted in similar effects on RNT and affect in daily life. Conclusions Results of this study imply that there was no additional benefit of having participants observe their thoughts detached and non-judgmentally, compared to excluding these assumed mechanisms of action as done for the active control group. We discuss possible reasons for the non-difference between the groups. Preregistration This study was preregistered at https://osf.io/rze64 .

stories.hook: ¿Podemos anticipar ataques de pánico con IA personalizada?
stories.headline: Modelos de aprendizaje automático personalizados predicen ataques de pánico en estudiantes universitarios
stories.finding: En una muestra longitudinal de 39 estudiantes universitarios durante seis meses, los modelos personalizados de regresión logística lograron un PR AUC lift de 1.17 sobre el azar (IC 95 %: 1.05‑1.25; p = .035). Estos modelos superaron al modelo generalizado (ratio = 1.18; p = .047).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la predicción individualizada de ataques de pánico es factible, lo que permitiría intervenciones preventivas tempranas y personalizadas, optimizando recursos clínicos y reduciendo la morbilidad asociada al trastorno.
stories.paperTitle: Development of personalized machine learning models for predicting panic attacks in college students
stories.originalAbstract: Panic attacks (PAs) are unexpected episodes of intense fear and anxiety, accompanied by cognitive and physical symptoms that significantly impair day-to-day functioning. This study proposes a machine learning approach to predict PA risk in the upcoming week in individuals across mental health conditions, enabling timely and potentially preventive mental health intervention. We evaluate the approach in a longitudinal sample of behavioral and physiological data collected using Oura rings from 39 college students over six months. We assessed multiple prediction algorithms applied within both personalized and generalized frameworks, fitting unique models for each participant and pooling data, respectively. Across all 39 participants, personalized models using logistic regression achieved a pooled PR AUC lift of 1.17 (95% CI: 1.05-1.25) over chance-level prediction (p = .035), whereas the generalized model did not differ from chance (PR AUC lift of 0.99; 95% CI: 0.90-1.08); in a direct comparison, personalized models outperformed the generalized model (lift ratio=1.18, p = .047). Performance varied across participants: when personalized models were grouped by unsupervised clustering of test-set PR AUC lift, models clustered as well-fit (n = 8) showed a pooled PR AUC lift of 2.26 (95% CI: 1.50-2.89) and models clustered as poor-fit (n = 31) a lift of 1.09 (95% CI: 0.98-1.17). Because these groups were defined by test-set performance, they describe observed heterogeneity and require validation in independent data. Together, our findings point towards the potential value of personalized modeling approaches and suggest that passively collected daily measurements of sleep, activity, and physiology may carry signal for predicting PAs, which could ultimately be leveraged to identify individually tailored lifestyle interventions to reduce PA risk.

stories.hook: ¿Los latidos monaurales pueden reducir la ansiedad mejor que la música sola?
stories.headline: Latidos monaurales de baja y moderada intensidad reducen ansiedad más que la música sola
stories.finding: En el estudio 1 con 207 participantes, los grupos con latidos monaurales de baja o moderada intensidad redujeron la ansiedad más que el grupo música‑solo (p = 0.047, β = ‑0.46), mientras que la alta intensidad disminuyó menos la ansiedad que la música‑solo.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la incorporación de estímulos auditivos sutiles puede potenciar intervenciones conductuales para la ansiedad, pero que una intensidad excesiva puede contrarrestar el beneficio, orientando el diseño de terapias basadas en música o neurofeedback.
stories.paperTitle: Music with monaural beats for anxiety reduction and mood enhancement in individuals with moderate trait-anxiety
stories.originalAbstract: Monaural beats embedded in music are a popular anxiety-relief intervention, yet implementation parameters and efficacy remain poorly understood. Across two studies of online participants with moderate trait anxiety, we tested whether theta-frequency (4–7 Hz) monaural beats in music produce anxiolytic and mood-enhancing effects beyond the same music alone, whether the salience of the beats relative to the music influences effects, and whether the effect of beats generalizes across heterogeneous musical stimuli. State anxiety, valence and arousal were measured before and after a 25-min listening period. In Study 1, participants (N = 207) were randomly assigned to hear music without beats (Music-Only control) or the same piece with monaural beats blended at three different salience levels: Low-, Moderate-, or High-Beatmix. The Low- and Moderate-Beatmix conditions yielded greater anxiety reductions than Music-Only (p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46, and p adjusted = 0.047, β = −0.46 respectively), whereas Music-Only reduced anxiety more than the High-Beatmix condition (p adjusted = 0.047, β = 0.42), indicating that overly salient beats might disrupt anxiolytic effects. Time × Condition interactions were not significant for valence or arousal. In Study 2, participants (N = 259) were randomized to one of four stylistically varied tracks, with or without beats at the Moderate-Beatmix level. Averaged across tracks, Beatmix conditions produced greater anxiety reductions (p < 0.0001, β = −0.49) and positive-valence increases (p = 0.029, β = 0.28) than Music-Only. As in Study 1, the Time × Condition interaction was nonsignificant for arousal. These studies provide some of the first evidence that adding monaural beats to music has anxiolytic effects beyond music alone, that efficacy depends on relative beat salience, and that findings replicate across a range of musical tracks.

stories.hook: ¿El tipo de adversidad determina la gravedad del trastorno?
stories.headline: Amenaza infantil predice mayor psicopatología que privación, según meta‑análisis
stories.finding: En una meta‑análisis preregistrada de 127 estudios (N = 163 767) se evaluaron las dimensiones de amenaza y privación y su relación con psicopatología interna, externa y específica de trauma en jóvenes. Los resultados mostraron que la dimensión de amenaza moderó significativamente las asociaciones, con efectos de mayor magnitud que la privación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que las intervenciones deben focalizarse en experiencias de amenaza para prevenir y tratar trastornos psicológicos, y que la distinción entre amenaza y privación es crucial en la evaluación del apego y el trauma.
stories.paperTitle: Do dimensions of childhood adversity differ in their direct associations with youth psychopathology? A meta-analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Growing evidence supports the unique pathways by which threat and deprivation, two core dimensions of adversity, confer risk for youth psychopathology. However, the extent to which these dimensions differ in their direct associations with youth psychopathology remains unclear. The primary aim of this preregistered meta-analysis was to synthesize the associations between threat, deprivation, internalizing, externalizing, and trauma-specific psychopathology. Because threat is proposed to be directly linked with socioemotional development, we hypothesized that the magnitude of associations between threat and psychopathology would be larger than those with deprivation. We conducted a search for peer-reviewed articles in English using PubMed and PsycINFO databases through August 2022. Studies that assessed both threat and deprivation and used previously validated measures of youth psychopathology were included. One hundred and twenty-seven articles were included in the synthesis (N = 163,767). Results of our three-level meta-analyses indicated that adversity dimension significantly moderated the associations between adversity and psychopathology, such that the magnitude of effects for threat (r's = .21-26) were consistently larger than those for deprivation (r's = .16-.19). These differences were more pronounced when accounting for the threat-deprivation correlation. Additional significant moderators included emotional abuse and youth self-report of adversity. Findings are consistent with the Dimensional Model of Adversity and Psychopathology, with clinical, research, and policy implications.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la falta de diversidad afecta la seguridad psicológica?
stories.headline: La escasa representación racial compromete la seguridad psicológica en terapia
stories.finding: En el Reino Unido, el 90 % de los psicólogos registrados se identifican como blancos, según datos de HCPC 2023. Esta homogeneidad limita la variedad de conocimientos y experiencias, dificultando la creación de entornos de seguridad psicológica para clientes de grupos históricamente excluidos.
stories.takeaway: Promover la diversidad racial y cultural entre los profesionales de la salud mental es esencial para ofrecer una atención equitativa y generar espacios terapéuticos seguros, lo que mejora la efectividad del tratamiento para poblaciones minoritarias.
stories.paperTitle: Navigating racial, ethnic and cultural differences in therapy: Therapists’ perspectives on the importance of psychological safety in training, supervision and practice
stories.originalAbstract: The UK population is becoming increasingly ethnically diverse (HM Government, 2024), yet the psychological workforce does not reflect this shift. According to HCPC (2023) data, 90% of registered practitioner psychologists identify as white, with figures echoed across counselling and psychotherapy (BACP, 2024; NHS England, 2023). This underrepresentation matters: a racially, ethnically, and culturally diverse workforce brings a broader range of knowledge, lived experiences, and perspectives, and representation at all levels of the profession supports organisations to better recognise and address the needs of historically excluded groups (Chouhan & Nazroo, 2020; McRae et al., 2025). Workforce diversity is therefore not only a matter of equity in employment but is essential for equitable mental healthcare (McRae et al., 2025), as global majority clients continue to face inequalities in mental healthcare (Bansal et al., 2022; Chan, 2023). However, increasing the representation of global majority therapists, while necessary, cannot be the only solution. The majority of the existing workforce is white, and research suggests that white therapists often lack sufficient knowledge, training, and confidence to sensitively manage conversations about racism (Samuel & Simonds, 2025). Although numerous frameworks and guidelines for ‘culturally competent’ practice exist (e.g., Comas-Díaz, 2012; Hays, 2016; Sue et al., 2019), there is limited evidence of engagement with them in practice (Worthington, 2007). Greater integration of racial, ethnic, and cultural themes across training and supervision is therefore needed for all therapists, regardless of background (Lee et al., 2021). Furthermore, research shows that global majority psychology and therapy trainees experience distress and marginalisation whilst navigating psychotherapeutic training (McCallum & Clarke, 2025), suggesting that existing training is not meeting the needs of white or global majority therapists and does not exemplify values of anti-racism or ‘cultural competence’. Research on ‘race’, ethnicity and culture in therapy has tended to focus either on the experiences of global majority clients (Bansal et al., 2022; Chan, 2023) or on the training needs (but not experiences) of white therapists (McRae et al., 2025; Samuel & Simonds, 2025). A smaller body of US and UK research has examined therapists’ experiences of working with racial/ethnic differences in therapy (Arundell et al., 2025; De Deus De Sousa et al. 2024; Dos Santos & Dallos, 2011; Faheem, 2023; Kanakam, 2021; Knox et al., 2003; Maxie et al., 2006; Spalding et al., 2018; Tummala-Narra et al. 2017) and shows that therapists’ are aware of the western and Eurocentric domination of the profession, and are able to reflect on ‘race’ and ethnicity in therapy. However, this research tends to focus on ‘cultural competence’ in therapy practice, particularly in the UK. Further research is needed to explore ‘race’, ethnicity and culture within training and supervision, and in practice from a relational stance that encourages therapists to reflect on their own positioning. Therefore, it is important to conduct research that includes therapists from any/all racial, ethnic and cultural backgrounds, from a range of different therapeutic modalities, so that a broad sense of the systemic issues surrounding ‘race’, ethnicity and culture within the therapy professions from the perspective of therapists can be better understood. Also, different modalities may approach ‘cultural competence’ in different ways. This study extends existing literature on therapists’ experiences by focusing on therapists’ perceptions of navigating racial, ethnic and cultural difference in therapy and exploring whether and how training and supervision have prepared them for and support them with this work. Data were generated using an online qualitative survey (Braun et al., 2020), and 59 therapists with a range of backgrounds responded to questions about their experiences of working with clients who occupy positions of racial, ethnic and cultural difference from themselves. The participant group – reflecting the wider therapeutic workforce – was predominantly white and female. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis (TA) (Braun & Clarke, 2022), informed by critical race theory (CRT) (Salter & Adams, 2013). Four themes were developed, with psychological safety as an overarching theme that was threaded throughout the analysis. Psychological safety is important for thinking about ‘race’, ethnicity and culture and racism within the therapy professions, as, for effective learning to occur, trainees, therapists and clients need to feel psychologically safe enough within the environment (Edmondson & Lei, 2014). The importance (and frequently, lack of) psychological safety in training and supervision is described in Theme 1 - Psychological safety is a prerequisite for meaningful discussions but is often lacking – in training and supervision. Theme 2 describes how the participants reported using their clinical skills to create safety with clients from a different racial, ethnic, or cultural background than themselves - How therapists create psychological safety across racial, ethnic and cultural difference. Predominantly white therapists’ fears around making mistakes and causing offence are captured in Theme 3 – The fear of getting it wrong leads to silence but also don’t get it wrong. And the role of racial, ethnic and cultural identities in therapy is captured in Theme 4 - Racial, ethnic and cultural identities inescapably matter in the therapeutic relationship. The findings highlight the critical role of psychological safety in therapy training, supervision and practice in relation to race, ethnicity and culture, as well as the consequences of its presence or absence. A key finding in the analysis was that a lack of psychological safety has distinct meanings and consequences for global majority and white therapists. This distinction shaped part of the analysis, as, for global majority participants, the threat of racial or ethnic discrimination is existential and continues outside of specific discussions about ‘race’, ethnicity and culture. In contrast, for white individuals, the sense of threat is predominantly brought about by discussions about ‘race’, ethnicity and culture, relating to the fear of being perceived as racist by others. Many participants found training programmes to be lacking in both content and process with regard to teaching on ‘race’, ethnicity and culture. The findings point to implications for training, supervision, and practice that are relevant across therapy disciplines in relation to decolonisation efforts, preparing trainee therapists for working across racial, ethnic and cultural difference, and the quality of care provided to global majority clients.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión potenciar la autorregulación emocional?
stories.headline: La autocompasión se asocia moderadamente con mejor autorregulación emocional y conductual
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de 107 estudios (N=49 189) encontró que la autocompasión se relaciona moderadamente a gran escala con la autorregulación adaptativa (r=.37) y negativamente con la autorregulación maladaptativa (r=‑.48). Los componentes de autocontrol (r=.38) y regulación emocional (r=.36) mostraron los efectos más fuertes.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que entrenar la autocompasión podría ser una estrategia eficaz para mejorar la regulación emocional en contextos clínicos y preventivos, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico respaldado por evidencia cuantitativa robusta.
stories.paperTitle: Self-compassion and self-regulation: A multilevel meta-analysis at composite, component, and individual subscale levels
stories.originalAbstract: Background. Despite accumulating evidence linking self-compassion to well-being and adaptive coping, how it relates to self-regulation remains largely examined at the meta-analytic level. Objectives. This meta-analysis examined associations between self-compassion and self-regulation dimensions at the composite, component, and individual subscale levels while testing three moderators: clinical status, mean age, and percentage of female participants. Method. A systematic search of PsycINFO, ERIC, and Web of Science identified 107 studies (N = 49,189). Multilevel random-effects meta-analysis with robust variance estimation was applied. Results. Composite self-compassion showed moderate-to-large associations with adaptive (r = .37) and maladaptive (r = − .48) self-regulation. Self-control (r = .38) and emotion regulation (r = .36) showed the strongest dimension-level effects, followed by goal pursuit (r = .21); self-reflection did not reach significance (r = .18, p = .083). Emotion dysregulation showed the largest single effect (r = − .47). At the component level, both positive and negative components significantly predicted self-regulation, with the negative component–maladaptive regulation association being strongest (r = .39). At the subscale level, all three positive components were significant whereas all three negative components were not. Higher female representation predicted stronger maladaptive associations but weaker self-control associations. Age moderated the negative component–adaptive regulation association. Clinical status did not meaningfully moderate any association. Conclusions. Each positive self-compassion component predicts self-regulation, representing unique regulatory resources, whereas negative components predict self-regulation only collectively, functioning as a unified uncompassionate orientation. Registration. This meta-analysis was pre-registered on PROSPERO (CRD1133033).

stories.hook: ¿Influye el reloj biológico en la depresión de pacientes con apnea?
stories.headline: Los genes del reloj circadiano se activan por la mañana en pacientes con apnea
stories.finding: En 184 sujetos, la expresión matutina de los genes circadianos BMAL1, CLOCK, PER1, CRY1 y NR1D1 fue mayor que la vespertina, excepto NPAS2. No hubo diferencias entre apnea (AHI > 5) y controles (AHI < 5), y la expresión matutina se asoció positivamente con la severidad depresiva.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la desregulación temporal de los genes del reloj, más que la gravedad de la apnea, está vinculada a la depresión, lo que abre la puerta a intervenciones cronobiológicas en OSA.
stories.paperTitle: Circadian clock dysregulation: a potential mechanism of depression in obstructive sleep apnea patients
stories.originalAbstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is characterized by co-occurrence with affective disorders. Our study aims to investigate the association of circadian clock gene expressions, and the presence and severity of depressive symptoms in OSA patients. The study included 184 individuals, who underwent polysomnography (PSG) and had their peripheral blood collected in the evening before and the morning after the PSG. Patients were divided into two groups: the OSA (apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) > 5) and the control group (AHI < 5). RNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. Expression levels of the selected genes (BMAL1, CLOCK, PER1, CRY1, NPAS2, and NR1D1) were assessed by qRT-PCR. Questionnaire data was collected in the morning (including the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Chronotype Questionnaire (CQ), and Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS)). The expression of all examined circadian clock genes in OSA patients was upregulated in the morning compared to the evening (except NPAS2). No differences were observed between OSA and control groups at either time point. Additionally, there was a positive correlation between the severity of depressive symptoms (assessed with MADRS) and morning expression of circadian genes in the group of OSA patients. Finally, in multivariable linear regression, ISI score (B = 0.750, p < 0.001), AM score of CQ (B = 0.416, p = 0.007), and morning PER1 gene expression (B = 4.310, p = 0.042) were found to be predictive factors for greater severity of depression symptoms in OSA patients. Dysregulated circadian clock gene expression in OSA patients is linked to depressive symptom severity, suggesting circadian disruption may underlie affective symptoms in OSA.

stories.hook: ¿Puede ACT mejorar la compasión en mujeres con enfermedad cardíaca?
stories.headline: ACT eleva la autocompasión y la tolerancia al malestar en mujeres con cardiopatías
stories.finding: Los resultados del análisis de covarianza mostraron una diferencia significativa entre los grupos experimental y de control en los puntajes de autocompasión y tolerancia al malestar tras la intervención. Esto sugiere que la terapia de aceptación y compromiso puede ser una intervención eficaz para mejorar estos constructos en mujeres con enfermedades cardiovasculares.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda la incorporación de ACT en programas de rehabilitación cardíaca, ofreciendo una herramienta breve y basada en evidencia para fortalecer la autocompasión y la tolerancia al estrés, factores asociados a mejor adherencia y pronóstico clínico.
stories.paperTitle: The Effectiveness of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy on Self-Compassion and Distress Tolerance in Women with Cardiovascular Diseases
stories.journal: Shenakht Journal of Psychology and Psychiatry
stories.originalAbstract: Purpose: Cardiovascular disease is one of the most common causes of death among non-communicable diseases. Objective: The present study was conducted to determine the effectiveness of acceptance and commitment therapy on distress tolerance and compassion in women with cardiovascular problems. Method: The research method was semi-experimental with a pre-test-post-test design with a control group. The statistical population consisted of female patients suffering from cardiovascular problems referred to the heart department of Imam Reza (AS) Amol Hospital in 1401-1402, 30 of whom were selected by available sampling method and divided into two treatment groups: acceptance and commitment (15 people) and control group (15). people) were placed. To collect data, Simon and Gaher (2005) distress tolerance scale and Neff (2003) compassion scale were used. The training group received Hayes et al.'s (2011) acceptance and commitment therapy for 8 sessions of 45 minutes. The data was analyzed using covariance analysis method with spss software version 22. Findings: The results of covariance analysis showed that there is a significant difference between the scores of the control and experimental groups (P=0.001). So that the treatment of acceptance and commitment led to an increase in distress tolerance and compassion in women with cardiovascular problems (P<0.05). Conclusion: Based on the obtained results, acceptance and commitment therapy was a suitable method to improve distress tolerance and compassion-exercise in women with cardiovascular problems. Due to the effectiveness of this method, it is suggested to be used along with other treatment methods to improve these variables in these women.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la terapia grupal elevar la autocompasión en adolescentes superdotados?
stories.headline: La terapia cognitivo-conductual grupal aumenta la autocompasión y reduce la inferioridad
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado con 24 adolescentes superdotados (12 experimental, 12 control), la terapia cognitivo-conductual grupal redujo significativamente depresión, ansiedad, estrés e inferioridad. También incrementó la autocompasión del grupo experimental, sin cambios en el control.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la intervención grupal basada en TCC es una herramienta eficaz para fortalecer la autocompasión y mitigar la sensación de inferioridad en jóvenes con altas capacidades, lo que puede prevenir trastornos emocionales y promover una autoestima saludable.
stories.paperTitle: Preliminary Results of the Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Group Therapy on Depression, Anxiety, Stress, Self-compassion, and Inferiority Feelings in Gifted Adolescents
stories.originalAbstract: Although gifted individuals are successful in areas requiring high cognitive performance, they may face many difficulties in social-emotional development and mental health. This study examined the effectiveness of Cognitive Behavioral Group Therapy (CBGT) on levels of depression, anxiety, stress, self-compassion, and inferiority among gifted adolescents. A total of 24 adolescents were randomly assigned to either an experimental group ( n = 12) or a control group ( n = 12). Data were collected using the Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scale (DASS-21), the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), and Inferiority Scale (IFS). CBGT program was applied to the experimental group, while no intervention was applied to the control group. One month after the end of the intervention program, a focus group interview was conducted with the participants. As a result of the study, it was determined that CBGT provided significant decreases in depression, anxiety, stress and inferiority scores and significant increases in self compassion scores of adolescents in the experimental group. On the other hand, there was no significant change in the depression, anxiety, stress, self compassion and inferiority scores of the control group. These results suggest that CBGT can be considered an effective intervention to improve mental health outcomes—such as reducing depression, anxiety, stress, and feelings of inferiority, while increasing self-compassion—thereby contributing to a broader construct of psychological well-being among gifted adolescents.

stories.hook: ¿El apoyo social protege del agotamiento físico?
stories.headline: El apoyo social atenúa el burnout por agotamiento emocional, no físico
stories.finding: En una muestra de 416 mujeres empleadas en pymes, el agotamiento físico y emocional reducen directamente el desempeño laboral. El burnout media completamente esa relación y el apoyo social debilita el vínculo entre agotamiento emocional y burnout, pero no entre agotamiento físico y burnout.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que las intervenciones organizacionales deben combinar apoyo social para mitigar el agotamiento emocional con medidas estructurales que reduzcan la carga física, optimizando así el desempeño de las mujeres en entornos laborales exigentes.
stories.paperTitle: The Dual Pathways of Work Stress: How Physical and Emotional Exhaustion Impair Female Employees' Performance Through Burnout
stories.journal: International Journal of Scientific and Management Research
stories.originalAbstract: This study examines how physical and emotional exhaustion affect female employees' work performance through the mediating role of job burnout, with social support as a moderator. Using a sample of 416 female employees from SMEs (92.44% response rate), we tested a model integrating five key factors: physical exhaustion, emotional exhaustion, job burnout, social support, and job performance. Regression analyses revealed three key findings: First, both physical and emotional exhaustion are directly impair performance; Second, job burnout fully mediates these relationships and third, social support buffers burnout's impact on performance and weakens the emotional exhaustion-burnout link, but not physical exhaustion effects. The results advance Job Burnout and Conservation of Resources theories by demonstrating gendered stress pathways in SMEs, where women face dual work-family pressures. Practically, the findings suggest organizations should combine structural interventions with psychological support systems, while recognizing social support's limited efficacy against physical strain. This study provides empirical evidence for developing gendersensitive wellbeing programs that address both physiological and psychological stress dimensions to sustain female employees' performance and wellbeing.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la familia extendida predecir la satisfacción marital?
stories.headline: Una nueva escala revela que la inserción familiar explica gran parte de la satisfacción conyugal
stories.finding: La Escala de Inserción Relacional (RES) de 31 ítems mostró consistencia interna excelente (α = .97) y validez convergente con la satisfacción marital (r = .61) en 957 cónyuges indios. La regresión jerárquica indicó que la RES explicó un 36 % de varianza adicional en la satisfacción, superando la influencia de la deseabilidad social (β = .60).
stories.takeaway: Este instrumento permite a terapeutas evaluar de forma fiable la influencia de la familia extendida en la dinámica conyugal, facilitando intervenciones focalizadas que consideren contextos colectivistas y mejoren la satisfacción marital.
stories.paperTitle: Development and validation of the Relational Embeddedness Scale (RES) in India.
stories.originalAbstract: In collectivistic cultures, marriage represents not merely a union between two individuals but a merging of two-family systems, with extended family relationships playing a role in marital satisfaction and stability. The present study developed and validated the Relational Embeddedness Scale (RES), a measure assessing extended family processes as a core determinant of marital functioning in collectivistic contexts. In a sample of 957 married individuals in India, exploratory factor analysis in a random split half (n = 455) revealed a unidimensional structure, subsequently confirmed through confirmatory factor analysis in the holdout sample (n = 502; CFI = .920, RMSEA = .062). The final 31-item scale demonstrated excellent internal consistency (α = .97) across genders, strong convergent validity with marital satisfaction (r = .61, p < .001), and good discriminant validity from social desirability (r = .06, ns). Hierarchical regression confirmed incremental validity, with the RES accounting for 36.0% additional variance in marital satisfaction beyond social desirability (β = .60, p < .001). Men reported higher levels of relational embeddedness (d = 0.17) and marital satisfaction (d = 0.24) than women, although the RES-satisfaction association did not differ significantly by gender. The unidimensional structure suggests that relational embeddedness constitutes a holistic relational experience in which in-law relationships, family support, and community integration form an integrated whole. The RES provides initial evidence of reliability and validity as an instrument for assessing family-embedded marital processes, with implications for both cross-cultural research on extended family systems and clinical work with couples in collectivistic contexts. stories.headline: Intervenciones psicológicas mejoran vulnerabilidades asociadas a la violencia en autistas
stories.finding: La evaluación rápida de evidencia analizó 18 estudios y halló que solo dos evaluaron intervenciones específicas para personas con trastorno del espectro autista. Los programas Diamant de resiliencia e integrative complexity mostraron mejoras modestamente consistentes en tolerancia a la ambigüedad, flexibilidad cognitiva y actitudes de extremismo violento.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de desarrollar y validar intervenciones psicológicas adaptadas a la neurodiversidad para prevenir conductas violentas, ofreciendo una guía preliminar para profesionales y políticas que aborden el riesgo de violencia en personas con autismo.
stories.paperTitle: Autism and lone-actor grievance-fueled violence: A rapid evidence assessment of best practice psychological treatment.
stories.journal: Journal of Threat Assessment and Management
stories.originalAbstract: Lone-actor grievance-fueled violence presents a growing challenge for security and mental health systems, with emerging evidence suggesting individuals with autism spectrum disorder may be disproportionately represented in this offender group. This rapid evidence assessment (REA) synthesizes current research on psychological interventions aimed at reducing lone-actor grievance-fueled violence risk in individuals with autism spectrum disorder. Eighteen studies were reviewed, but only two directly evaluated interventions tailored for autistic individuals. Most studies were methodologically weak, lacked manualized interventions, and offered limited empirical data. Programs such as the Diamant resilience intervention and integrative complexity showed promising results with modest but consistent improvements in autism spectrum disorder-specific vulnerabilities such as tolerance of ambiguity , cognitive flexibility , and attitudes associated with violent extremism. The findings highlight a critical need for high-quality, trauma-informed, neurodiversity affirming research to guide clinical practice , policy, and future intervention development to ethically and effectively address the risk of lone-actor grievance-fueled violence in neurodivergent individuals.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué los diseños digitales nos vuelven adictos?
stories.headline: Los diseños online adictivos comprometen el bienestar del usuario
stories.finding: El informe reúne evidencia robusta sobre cómo ciertos rasgos de diseño capturan la atención y maximizan el compromiso, explotando mecanismos psicológicos como el refuerzo intermitente. Además, evalúa la efectividad limitada de medidas regulatorias actuales para mitigar estos riesgos.
stories.takeaway: Comprender estos mecanismos permite a profesionales de salud mental y a políticos diseñar intervenciones y regulaciones que protejan la salud psicológica frente a la sobreexposición digital.
stories.originalAbstract: This report presents the issue of addictive online design, aimed at captivating attention and maximising user engagement. It discusses the business model that incentivises this practice, common addictive design features, the psychological mechanisms that underpin their effectiveness, potential problematic uses of digital technology that might result from it, the potential risks to user wellbeing, and what is known about the effectiveness of different policy measures. It gathers robust evidence from a range of perspectives to inform policymakers on the latest knowledge, including gaps and points of debate.

stories.hook: ¿Qué tan frecuente el PTSD tras un terremoto adolescente?
stories.headline: Alto 18,5% de adolescentes presentan PTSD tras sismo
stories.finding: El estudio encuestó a 551 adolescentes de 13 a 17 años tras el terremoto de Cianjur; 18,5% cumplieron criterios de PTSD y 6,9% de PGD. El análisis de regresión mostró que los síntomas de PTSD se asociaron significativamente con menores puntuaciones de bienestar mental.
stories.takeaway: Estos datos subrayan la necesidad de intervenciones tempranas de salud mental para adolescentes tras desastres, enfocándose en el PTSD para prevenir deterioro del bienestar psicológico.
stories.paperTitle: Post-traumatic stress disorder and prolonged grief disorder among adolescents after the cianjur earthquake: prevalence and mental health implications
stories.originalAbstract: The Cianjur earthquake on November 21, 2022, caused severe psychological impacts, particularly among adolescents who experienced significant loss or direct exposure to the disaster. This study aimed to analyze the prevalence of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) and Prolonged Grief Disorder (PGD), and to examine their respective effects on the mental health of adolescent disaster survivors. The research employed a descriptive and correlational quantitative design using a survey approach. A total of 551 adolescents aged 13–17 were selected through purposive sampling based on their exposure to the disaster’s impact. Three instruments were used to collect data: the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) to assess post-disaster trauma symptoms; the PGD-13-R to measure prolonged grief severity; and the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form (MHC-SF) to evaluate emotional, psychological, and social well-being. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression. Results showed that 18.5% of respondents met the criteria for PTSD and 6.9% for PGD. Regression analysis indicated that PTSD had a significant negative impact on mental health (β = –0.250; p < 0.001), while PGD was not a significant predictor (β = 0.046; p = 0.312). These findings suggest that post-disaster trauma contributes more substantially to mental health deterioration than prolonged grief. Therefore, evidence-based interventions such as Ego State Therapy are recommended to address PTSD symptoms effectively among adolescents affected by the earthquake.

Three instruments were used to collect data: the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) to assess post-disaster trauma symptoms; the PGD-13-R to measure prolonged grief severity; and the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form (MHC-SF) to evaluate emotional, psychological, and social well-being. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, Pearson correlations, and multiple linear regression. Results showed that 18.5% of respondents met the criteria for PTSD and 6.9% for PGD. Regression analysis indicated that PTSD had a significant negative impact on mental health (β = –0.250; p < 0.001), while PGD was not a significant predictor (β = 0.046; p = 0.312). These findings suggest that post-disaster trauma contributes more substantially to mental health deterioration than prolonged grief. Therefore, evidence-based interventions such as Ego State Therapy are recommended to address PTSD symptoms effectively among adolescents affected by the earthquake.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el ejercicio mejorar la atención en adolescentes con dificultades de aprendizaje?
stories.headline: Ejercicio aeróbico supera a la NLP en atención sostenida
stories.finding: Se evaluó a 45 adolescentes (13‑15 años) con discapacidades de aprendizaje, asignados aleatoriamente a ejercicio aeróbico, NLP o control durante dos meses. El análisis de medidas repetidas mostró mejoras significativas en la atención sostenida y funciones ejecutivas en los grupos de ejercicio y NLP respecto al control.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que intervenciones físicas o cognitivas pueden potenciar la atención en jóvenes con dificultades de aprendizaje, ofreciendo alternativas no farmacológicas para mejorar el rendimiento académico y reducir el impacto del TDAH.
stories.paperTitle: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Aerobic Exercise Training and Neuro-Linguistic Programming (NLP) Strategies on Executive Functions in Students with Learning Disabilities
stories.journal: The Psychological Research in Individuals with Exceptional Needs
stories.originalAbstract: The present study aimed to compare the effectiveness of aerobic exercise training and neuro-linguistic programming (NLP) strategies on sustained attention, planning, and organization in students with learning disabilities. This quasi-experimental study employed a pretest–posttest design with a control group and a two-month follow-up. The statistical population consisted of students with learning disabilities attending educational and clinical centers in the Mehrshahr district of Karaj during the 2024–2025 academic year. Using convenience sampling, 45 eligible students aged 13–15 years were selected and randomly assigned to three groups: aerobic exercise training (n = 15), NLP strategies training (n = 15), and control (n = 15). The two experimental groups received their respective interventions over a two-month period, whereas the control group received no intervention. Executive functions were assessed using the Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function, Teacher Form (BRIEF), at pretest, posttest, and follow-up. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons in SPSS version 26. Repeated-measures analysis showed significant time and group effects for sustained attention (F = 31.804, p < .001, partial η² = .602; F = 18.720, p < .001, partial η² = .471), planning (F = 63.613, p < .001, partial η² = .752; F = 7.289, p = .002, partial η² = .258), and organization (F = 62.953, p < .001, partial η² = .623; F = 6.405, p = .004, partial η² = .234). Bonferroni comparisons indicated that both aerobic exercise and NLP significantly improved sustained attention and planning compared with the control group, while no significant difference was found between the two interventions. For organization, only the NLP group differed significantly from the control group (p = .003), whereas aerobic exercise did not (p = .630). Both aerobic exercise training and NLP strategies can improve sustained attention and planning in students with learning disabilities, while NLP strategies may offer a more specific benefit for organizational functioning.

stories.hook: ¿Influye el orden de nacimiento en la salud mental adolescente?
stories.headline: Primogénitos muestran peor salud mental y menos calor parental bajo la política de tres hijos
stories.finding: En un estudio transversal con 3581 adolescentes chinos, los primogénitos obtuvieron puntuaciones más altas en el SDQ total (β=0.74, p<0.01) y en síntomas emocionales, de conducta y de relación con pares. Además, recibieron menos estilos parentales cálidos y de confianza (β=-0.54 y β=-0.34, p<0.001).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que el orden de nacimiento, en el contexto de la política de tres hijos, afecta la vulnerabilidad psicológica de los adolescentes, lo que implica la necesidad de intervenciones focalizadas en los primogénitos y en la promoción de estilos parentales cálidos.
stories.paperTitle: Birth Order and Chinese Adolescent Mental Health within the Context of the Three-Child Policy: The Roles of Parenting Styles and Parental Company
stories.originalAbstract: Purpose: The implementation of the three-child policy brings about changes to family structures and resource distributions. However, little research has explored the effects of birth order on adolescent mental health in this context. This study aims to bridge the gap by investigating the relationship between birth order and mental health and discovering the underlying factors. Patients and Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 3581 adolescents from 42 schools across 17 cities in China were recruited. Data on mental health (the adapted Chinese version of the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, SDQ), parenting styles (the Parenting Styles Scale), birth order, duration of parental company, and demographic characteristics were assessed. Hierarchical multiple regression analysis analyzes the relationships among these factors. Results: Compared with only-child adolescents, first-borns had higher scores of total SDQ (β= 0.74, p<0.01), emotional symptoms (β= 0.22, p<0.05), conduct symptoms (β= 0.18, p<0.01), and peer relationship symptoms (β= 0.29, p<0.001). They experienced less emotionally warm (β= -0.54, p<0.001) and trust-encouraged (β= -0.34, p<0.01) parenting styles, with shorter durations of parental company (β= -0.26, p<0.001). Middle-born adolescents had higher peer relationship symptoms scores and more neglectful parenting styles. Last-born adolescents were more likely to receive spoiled parenting styles. Conclusion: This study elucidates the effects of birth order on adolescent mental health in the three-child policy era, revealing that parenting styles vary by birth order. First-borns may experience suboptimal parenting styles and shorter parental company, increasing mental health risks. Middle-borns may encounter neglectful parenting styles, while last-borns experience spoiled parenting styles. These findings emphasize the need for tailored support from parents and schools to address each child's unique needs and foster better psychological development. Limitations include reliance on self-reported data and the cross-sectional design that restricts causal inference. Future research should adopt longitudinal designs and explore cultural and regional variations.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el ejercicio revertir el dolor crónico mediante el cerebro?
stories.headline: El ejercicio activa circuitos mesocorticolímbicos y alivia el dolor crónico
stories.finding: El ejercicio libera miokinas, como IGF‑1, que estimulan neuronas orexínicas e impulsan la vía dopaminérgica del sistema de recompensa. En modelos, el ejercicio activó neuronas de la amígdala basal que proyectan al núcleo accumbens y la inhibición de GABAérgicos en la amígdala central disminuyó la congelación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que el ejercicio puede modular circuitos de recompensa y miedo, ofreciendo una intervención no farmacológica para el manejo del dolor crónico y sus comorbilidades emocionales.
stories.paperTitle: Exercise therapy for chronic pain: an updated perspective on mesocorticolimbic system function
stories.originalAbstract: ABSTRACT: Patients with chronic pain often experience behavioral issues linked to pain, depression, and other emotional disorders. These problems stem from dysfunction in the mesocorticolimbic system, and exercise offers a safe, accessible, and effective alternative. It not only reduces pain but also activates multiple neural pathways, helping restore normal function. First, in the periphery, exercise promotes the release of myokines, which are essential for the body-brain connection and influence neural activity. IGF-1, released from muscles during exercise, can cross the blood-brain barrier and affect the brain. IGF-1 specifically targets orexin neurons in the hypothalamus, which then stimulate dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area, triggering the reward system. Second, exercise can reshape neural circuits and restore mesocorticolimbic function, reducing chronic pain and related issues. We showed that exercise activates neurons in the basal nucleus of the amygdala that project to the nucleus accumbens, supporting patients' goal-directed behavior. Moreover, inhibiting GABAergic neurons in the central nucleus of the amygdala decreases freezing behavior. Third, chronic pain often leads to depression, mainly due to reduced activity of serotonin (5-HT) neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus, which impairs the brain's reward system. Exercise boosts activity of 5-HT neurons in the dorsal raphe nucleus. Furthermore, exercise can modify gene expression through epigenetic mechanisms, leading to long-lasting improvements in brain function and behavior. Overall, exercise can restore brain function, helping individuals overcome chronic pain and lead healthier lives. These findings support exercise therapy as a key component of chronic pain management and suggest mesocorticolimbic mechanisms underlying its effects.
